title.narrative: RESILAND Niger Integrated Landscape Management Project

description.narrative: The development objective of Integrated Landscape Management Project for is to increase the adoption of climate smart landscape restoration practices and improve access to income earning opportunities in targeted communes in Niger. This project has three components. 1) The first component, Knowledge Creation and Territorial Planning for Climate Resilience, has the following sub-components: (i) National forest and pastoral lands inventory; (ii) Development of forest, pastoral areas, and fisheries management plans; (iii) Climate informed territorial planning and development in targeted Communes; and (iv) Enabling environment for Niger Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) implementation. 2) The second component, Investments in Landscape Restoration and Community Resilience to Climate Change, has the following sub-components: (i) Restoring Landscapes and Ecosystem Services; and (ii) Improving Local Livelihoods Resilience. 3) The third component, Project Coordination, Monitoring and Communication, has the following components: (i) Project coordination and management; (ii) Project monitoring and evaluation (M&E); and (iii) Project communication and conflict management. 4) The fourth component, Contingent Emergency Response, would allow the government to request to re-categorize and reallocate financing from other project components to partially cover emergency response and recovery costs.

To increase the adoption of climate smart landscape restoration practices and improve access to income earning opportunities in targeted communes in Niger and also enhance regional knowledge sharing and climate services in Sahel countries.

To date, 80 forest management plans (151,994 ha), 24 aquatic management plans (2,398 ha), and 6 pastoral management plans (748 km equivalent to 19, 401 ha) have been adopting, bringing the total of hectares brought under management plans to 173,793.
An additional 21 forest management plans covering 20,427 hectares are currently under development. 11 other FMP covering 65,444 ha are awaiting no-objections. The final 20 FMP planned for the year are awaiting development of TORs. Under aquatic management plans, an additional 10 covering 850 hectares are currently being developed. These are expected to be completed by the end of 2026 and the annual target is likely to be exceeded.
A variety of communication products have been produced. Accelerated progress is expected now that the Communications Specialist is recruited.

title.narrative: Land area under sustainable landscape management practices

comment.narrative:
To date, 116,841 hectares are under SLM, and 2,380 km2 of firebreaks have been built to protect 257,040 ha of grazing land, for a total of 373,881 hectares under SLM.

Additionally, to harmonize projects across the portfolio, inclusion of hectares protected by firebreaks follows measurement of this indicator by other projects.

title.narrative: Land users adopting sustainable land management practices

comment.narrative: A total of 110,816 heads of household have been mobilized for SLM activities. Based on the context, the project assumes that the practices will be shared with and adopted by other members of the same household. On the basis of the average composition of a household in Niger (7 people), 782,712 people are considered to have adopted the practices in the first rounds of SLM activities. This indicator reports to PROGREEN under the AF and the target is 40,000 people, 12,000 of which are women. A survey will be done during the mid-term review of the project to update this number.
